findingDetails.title: The reference calls all six post_tool bindings non-strict while one of them is declared strict, and the same document says a strict post_tool failure clears the tool result
findingDetails.scopeProof: :37 is the only sentence in the document that states the strictness of the post_tool set, and hooks.toml:91 is the only strict line among the six post_tool entries
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: a corrected :37 that reads seven strict pre_tool guards and one strict post_tool check

findingDetails.title: The reply table names only decision/reason as a conforming object and calls every other shape a schema mismatch, while eight of the bundle's own hooks reply with hook_specific_output.additional_context
findingDetails.scopeProof: :203-212 is the only reply table in the document, and the eight call sites are the complete set of hook_specific_output emitters in the bundle
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: a reply table that lists hook_specific_output.additional_context as a conforming object for the types that accept it

findingDetails.title: The shared tool-name seam keys process_start on the bare spelling only, while the fixture states every tool_name is qualified and one guard already hedges both spellings
findingDetails.scopeProof: hook-io.mjs:33-39 is the only tool-name map in the bundle, and deep-loop-guard.mjs:32 is the only other place a Vibe tool name is matched against a set
findingDetails.downgradeTrigger: a captured process_start payload showing the bare tool_name, or a CORE_TOOL_NAMES entry that lists both spellings

results.summary: The 18-binding census matches hooks.toml on every count and the 21-row classification names only bindings that exist. Two claims fail: the post_tool strictness adjective at :37 (raised as R3-P2-001) and the fixture's always-qualified statement against the bare process_start key (raised as R3-P2-003).
The declared target is a file set, not a spec folder with a checklist; the disposition table is an exclusion list, not a checklist to verify.

The document's claim that the turn-start composer routes the advisor under the vibe label is carried by turn-start.mjs and prompt-advisor.mjs, and the session_start goal bridge claim is carried by session-start.mjs. No mismatch.

Each Vibe adapter checked against its OpenCode counterpart for a dropped behaviour. overlay-guard and session-cleanup remain the only two parity defects, already recorded as R1-P2-005 and R1-P2-004. The remaining differences are the documented intentional ones.
No feature catalogue covers this file set.
The playbook's hook-scenario verdict table is the live-verdict surface and this iteration read no scenario file. Carried to the residual sweep.

noveltyJustification: weightedNew = 3 (three P2) against weightedTotal 16, the accumulated active set after this iteration (1 P1 = 5, 11 P2 = 11). No prior finding was refined or repeated: two findings are document claims that fail against the file they describe, and the third is a name-mapping gap distinct from R1-P1-001's tool_input key. The iteration also records a self-correction of a citation made in iteration 2.

searchLedger.rationale: three-way self-contradiction in the document with a named behavioural consequence at :214

searchActions.queryOrPath: hook_specific_output across the repo-guards scripts and the vibe adapters
searchActions.result: eight production emitters, none of them listed in the reply table at :203-212, while the same document uses the field in prose at :130, :131, :135, :155 and :238

searchLedger.rationale: the table and the prose disagree, and the live evidence is on the bundle's side

searchLedger.hypothesis: the tool-name map is keyed on a spelling the fixture says cannot occur

searchActions.result: the fixture says tool_name is always qualified and then names process_start bare; the map holds four qualified keys and one bare key; deep-loop-guard hedges four spellings for the spawn tool

searchLedger.rationale: the bundle already hedges the ambiguity at one site and not at the shared seam

searchLedger.hypothesis: the missing match selector makes the hook fire on every tool call for no reason

searchActions.result: coreToolNameFor returns null for any name that is not mcp_<server>.<tool>, and main allows before the core runs; Vibe's MCP tool names are dynamic so no static selector could express them

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: the hook filters to MCP names before the core runs, and the names cannot be enumerated in a static selector

searchLedger.hypothesis: a Vibe adapter drops a behaviour its OpenCode counterpart has

searchActions.queryOrPath: the 21-row classification against hooks.toml, plus overlay-guard.js:80-125 and session-cleanup.js:112-375
searchActions.result: every row's Vibe event column names a binding that exists; the only two parity defects are the ones already recorded as R1-P2-004 and R1-P2-005; the remaining differences are documented as intentional at :133-135

searchLedger.ruledOutReason: no new parity gap; the two known ones are already recorded
